per_case.answer_text:
Short version
- Join the OpenChat proposals group to view and discuss proposals (use the group link in the app). Read the governance blog post for a step‑by‑step guide.
- The easiest way to vote is from within the OpenChat app; voting will also be supported from the NNS dapp later.

What you need to know and do
1) Eligibility: to vote a neuron must exist and have a dissolve delay of at least 1 month when the proposal was made. (Only eligible neurons count.)
2) How voting works: voting power = stake × dissolve‑delay bonus × age bonus. The dissolve‑delay bonus ranges from 1 (zero delay) up to 2 (one year); the age bonus ranges from 1 (zero age) up to 1.25 (6 months age). Example: a 1000 CHAT stake with 1 year dissolve delay and 6 months age has voting power 2500.
3) How proposals pass: after 4 days (or a period of quiet) the sum of “adopt” votes must exceed “reject” votes, and “adopt” must have at least 3% of total voting power. The vote ends immediately if either side exceeds 50% of available voting power. You can still participate during the 4‑day period even if the proposal has already resolved (so neurons can earn voting rewards).
4) If you used the decentralisation sale / NNS dapp: your CHAT neurons are controlled by your NNS dapp principal. Before voting from OpenChat you must add your OpenChat User Id as a hot‑key for your neurons. To find your OpenChat User Id: open the app menu → Profile settings → Advanced (bottom). Then in the NNS dapp go to My Neuron Staking → select OpenChat → select your neuron (if neurons are set to follow the oldest, select that neuron) → Add Hotkey → paste your OpenChat User Id. If your neurons follow your oldest neuron you only need to add the hot‑key to that neuron.

Where to start
- Join the OpenChat proposals group and read the governance blog post for the full step‑by‑step guide and links.

If you want, tell me whether you vote from OpenChat or from the NNS dapp and I’ll list the exact menu steps again.

grade.rationale: All major claims (where to start, voting method, eligibility, voting power formula and bonuses, proposal passing rules, and NNS hotkey steps) are explicitly supported by the cited FAQ and governance blog chunks, and are accurately stated. The answer includes relevant citations and appropriately answers an answerable question.

Short answer: not fully end-to-end encrypted yet.

Currently OpenChat runs on the Internet Computer, which provides strong platform-level security, but there is a known risk that a rogue node operator could intercept ingress messages or read memory. Once SEV‑SNP is available on node machines, users can be much more confident that their data won’t be accessible to others. The team also plans to implement end-to-end (e2e) encryption in future so that canister data would be stored encrypted (likely as an opt‑in feature for selected chats and with some limitations such as reduced searchability). Note that message text and thumbnails are stored in per‑user or per‑group canisters and file data is kept in OpenStorage (storage limits and retention rules apply).

per_case.answer_text:
The 100,000 CHAT airdrop is split into two pots: 80,000 CHAT distributed proportionally by “shares”, and 20,000 CHAT distributed by lottery.

- Shares pot (80,000 CHAT): you get 1 share for every 5,000 CHIT you have. Your payout from this pot = 80,000 × (your shares) ÷ (total shares across all entrants). Example from the blog: 36,500 CHIT → 7 shares; if there are 10,000 shares in total you would get 80,000 × 7 / 10,000 = 56 CHAT. Because the pot is fixed, your amount falls as more users enter.

- Lottery pot (20,000 CHAT): normally you receive 1 lottery ticket for every 25,000 CHIT. (Prizes were originally 12,000, 5,000 and 3,000 CHAT.) For the end-of-August airdrop the rules were changed so participants with at least 25,000 CHIT or a 30-day streak get a single ticket; 10 tickets are drawn and each winner receives 2,000 CHAT.

Note: you must enter via the CHIT for CHAT community (gated as described) and your current CHIT balance determines your airdrop share; current CHIT is reset to zero after each airdrop.

grade.rationale: All details about the 80k shares pot, 20k lottery, the example calculation, the end-of-August lottery rule change, entry via the CHIT for CHAT community, and current CHIT reset are directly supported by the cited blog chunks. The answer is accurate, uses relevant citations, and appropriately answers an answerable question.

per_case.answer_text:
Short answer

Voting rewards are minted by the SNS and distributed as “maturity” to neurons that participated in voting. For each proposal ballot, a neuron’s reward for that ballot is proportional to its voting power relative to the total voting power of all participating (eligible) neurons. Rewards are generated at a rate of 2.5% of total token supply annually and are distributed daily, accounting for all ballots that ended that day (if no ballots end that day rewards carry over).

Key details

- Eligibility: a neuron must exist and have a dissolve delay of at least 1 month at the time the proposal was made to be eligible to vote and earn rewards.
- Voting power (used to split rewards) = stake × dissolve-delay bonus × age bonus. The dissolve-delay bonus runs from 1 (0 delay) up to 2 (1 year delay). The age bonus runs from 1 (0 age) up to 1.25 (6 months of age); age resets to 0 when the neuron starts dissolving. Example: 1,000 CHAT with 1 year dissolve delay and 6 months’ age → voting power = 2,500.
- If you fail to vote on a proposal you do not earn voting rewards for that proposal (so users who cannot vote manually may configure neurons to follow trusted voters).
- Maturity earned can be disbursed (minting CHAT into the account) or staked/auto‑staked to grow the neuron.

(Also: proposal adoption rules and vote finishing mechanics determine which ballots end and therefore which ballots are counted for daily reward distribution.)

grade.rationale: The answer matches the cited governance docs: rewards accrue as maturity, are proportional to voting power, distributed daily with carryover, total annual rate is 2.5%, eligibility and voting power formula (stake × dissolve-delay × age) and bonuses are correct, and not voting yields no rewards. The provided citations directly support these claims.

per_case.answer_text:
The dev team beacon neuron is a small, public neuron the OpenChat devs configured as a “beacon” for others to follow. It follows each dev-team member’s neurons and will cause followers to vote the same way when a majority of the dev team vote alike. Its neuron id is 9adf350c7388dfe7277213a5fc8d817c2d5bc6ff6be5870f0d33d9d6dab01fc6. The devs removed its controller so the beacon itself is immutable and cannot vote independently.

Whether you should follow it depends on your preference: if you’re happy to follow the dev team’s lead you can follow this beacon to implicitly participate in every vote and thus maximise voting rewards. If you want more control you can follow the beacon on the catch‑all (Unspecified) topic but exclude specific topics (for example motions, token transfers, SNS parameter changes) by configuring your neuron to follow itself on those topics. If you have multiple neurons, it’s common to set younger ones to follow your eldest and manage more nuanced following on the eldest.

grade.rationale: The answer closely reflects the cited governance docs: it describes the beacon neuron, its ID, majority-follow behavior, controller removal/immutability, reward maximization, topic exclusions via following oneself, and multi‑neuron follow practice. The provided citations are relevant to each claim and the question was properly answered.
